lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach aquatic whorled dissected foliage plus tiny epigynous flowers and an inferior ovary that splits into one-seeded mericarps.

project_scope.note: The pool contains Myriophyllum heterophyllum, native in Texas under current Kew, and M. aquaticum, introduced in Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: In the project genus, start with submerged leaves arranged in whorls and deeply pinnately divided into threadlike segments. Then inspect the emergent flowering region for tiny flowers above an inferior 2–4-locular ovary.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Aquatic or amphibious herbs; Myriophyllum usually has whorled submerged leaves that are pinnatisect/pectinate into fine segments.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers very small, commonly 4-merous and unisexual or bisexual. In Myriophyllum, lower flowers are usually pistillate and upper flowers staminate. Ovary inferior, commonly 4-celled with one ovule per locule.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Schizocarp or nutlet-like fruit separating into usually 4 one-seeded mericarps.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Whorled feather-like aquatic leaves + tiny emergent flowers + inferior ovary + 4-part mericarp fruit = project Haloragaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whorled submerged leaf → emergent flowering spike → male-above/female-below → inferior ovary → 4 mericarps → native/introduced split
visual_lesson.intro: Water-milfoils look like foliage plants until you notice the tiny reproductive zone rising from the water.

steps.title: 1 · Read the whorled feather-like leaf
steps.look_for: Several leaves per node, each divided into many threadlike side segments.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fastest project-level Myriophyllum recognition cue.

steps.title: 2 · Follow the stem above the water
steps.look_for: Upper leaves reduce toward bracts and tiny flowers appear in their axils.
steps.why_it_matters: The reproductive zone is easily missed because the flowers are so small.

steps.title: 3 · Learn the sex arrangement
steps.look_for: Pistillate flowers commonly lower on the spike and staminate flowers above.
steps.why_it_matters: This provides a memorable reproductive architecture rather than relying on foliage alone.

steps.title: 4 · Confirm the inferior ovary and 4 mericarps
steps.look_for: Inferior 4-celled ovary maturing into four one-seeded units.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest family-level reproductive confirmation.

steps.title: 5 · Keep native and introduced species separate
steps.look_for: M. heterophyllum is native in Texas; M. aquaticum is South American and introduced in Texas.
steps.why_it_matters: Field recognition should not accidentally turn an invasive aquatic into a native restoration target.

comparisons.title: Haloragaceae vs Ceratophyllaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have finely divided submerged whorled leaves. Myriophyllum has a distinct emergent floral zone and inferior ovary/mericarp fruit; Ceratophyllum has forked leaves and very different reproductive structures.

comparisons.title: Haloragaceae vs Cabombaceae
comparisons.rule: Cabomba has opposite/whorled fanlike leaves and showier floating/emergent flowers; Myriophyllum has featherlike pinnatisect leaves and minute axillary flowers.

visual_lesson.caveat: Aquatic leaf form is plastic. Confirm flower/fruit characters whenever possible.

genera.fast_cue: whorled pinnatisect aquatic leaves + tiny emergent flowers + inferior 4-celled ovary + 4 mericarps
